title: Problem Overview
content: **Erdős Problem #136** asks for the Erdős-Gyárfás function f(n,4,5): the minimum number of colors to edge-color Kₙ so every K₄ has at least 5 different colors among its 6 edges. Erdős-Gyárfás proved (5/6)(n-1) < f(n) < n and computed f(9) = 8. Bennett et al. (2022) and Joos-Mubayi (2022) independently proved f(n) ~ (5/6)n, confirming the lower bound is tight.
mathContext: f(n,p,q) = min{k : ∃ edge k-coloring of Kₙ with every Kₚ using ≥ q colors}. Here p=4, q=5. K₄ has C(4,2) = 6 edges, so requiring ≥ 5 colors means at most one repeated color per K₄.

title: Coloring Definitions
content:
Four definitions form the foundation. **EdgeColoring n k** assigns a color from Fin k to each pair of vertices. **isValidColoring** ensures symmetry (c i j = c j i). **colorsInK4** collects the 6 edge colors of a 4-clique into a Finset. **hasAtLeast5ColorsInEveryK4** is the global constraint: every injective mapping of 4 vertices yields a K₄ with ≥ 5 distinct colors.

The injective mapping formulation quantifies over all C(n,4) possible 4-cliques.
mathContext: colorsInK4 c v = {c(v₀,v₁), c(v₀,v₂), c(v₀,v₃), c(v₁,v₂), c(v₁,v₃), c(v₂,v₃)} — all 6 edges of K₄.

title: The Erdős-Gyárfás Function f(n)
content:
**f_exists** axiomatizes that for any n, there exists some k-coloring satisfying the K₄ constraint (trivially, n colors work). **f(n)** is then defined as Nat.find applied to f_exists, yielding the minimum such k.

The definition is noncomputable because Nat.find uses Classical.choice.
mathContext: f(n) = Nat.find(f_exists n) = min{k : ∃ valid k-coloring with K₄ constraint}.

title: Erdős-Gyárfás Bounds
content:
Three axioms capture the original results. **erdos_gyarfas_lower_bound**: f(n) > (5/6)(n-1) for n ≥ 4. **erdos_gyarfas_upper_bound**: f(n) < n for n ≥ 4. **f_9**: f(9) = 8, a concrete computation.

The lower bound suggests f(n) ~ (5/6)n, which turned out to be correct. The upper bound f(n) < n is loose.

title: The 2022 Asymptotic Resolution
content:
**bcdp_asymptotic**: f(n)/n → 5/6 as n → ∞, expressed via Filter.Tendsto to nhds(5/6). This is the main resolution of Problem #136. **AsymptoticResult** gives the equivalent ε-δ formulation: for all ε > 0, eventually |f(n)/n - 5/6| < ε. **asymptotic_holds** axiomatizes this equivalent form.

Bennett, Cushman, Dudek, and Pralat proved this in 2022. Joos and Mubayi found an independent shorter proof via hypergraph matchings.
mathContext: lim_{n→∞} f(n)/n = 5/6. Equivalently: ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N₀, ∀ n ≥ N₀, |f(n)/n - 5/6| < ε.

title: Why 5/6?
content:
Two proved theorems explaining the constant. **why_five_sixths**: 6-1=5 and 5/6 = 1 - 1/6 (proved by norm_num). **k4_edges**: Nat.choose 4 2 = 6 (proved by norm_num).

The constant 5/6 emerges naturally: K₄ has 6 edges, we require 5 colors, so the defect tolerance is 1/6, giving the asymptotic ratio 5/6.
mathContext: C(4,2) = 6 edges in K₄. Requiring ≥ 5 colors means tolerance = 1/6. Asymptotic ratio = 1 - 1/6 = 5/6.

title: Related Values and Monotonicity
content:
**small_values**: f(4) = 5, f(5) = 5, f(6) = 5, f(9) = 8. These concrete values illustrate the function's behavior for small n. **f_nondecreasing**: f is monotone non-decreasing, since adding vertices to Kₙ can only increase the minimum colors needed.

The small values show that f grows slowly initially, consistent with f(n) ~ (5/6)n.
